stem: The table shows the 200 members of a gym, by type of membership and preferred time to exercise. If a member who prefers to exercise in the evening is selected at random, what is the probability that the member has an annual membership?

figure.title: Gym members by membership type and preferred time

solution: The condition is “prefers the evening,” so the denominator is the Evening total: 110.
Annual members who prefer the evening: 48.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This divides by all 200 members, giving the probability that a member has an annual membership AND prefers the evening.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the probability that a randomly selected member has an annual membership; it ignores the condition.
explanation.C: Correct. Of the 110 members who prefer the evening, 48 have an annual membership.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This divides by the 80 annual members, giving the probability that an annual member prefers the evening: the condition is reversed.

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'A': 'A', 'B': 'B', 'C': 'C', 'D': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'A', 'B': 'B', 'C': 'C', 'D': 'D'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
r = {row[0]: [int(v) for v in row[1:]] for row in figure['rows']}
assert r['Monthly'][1] + r['Annual'][1] == r['Total'][1]
p = Rational(r['Annual'][1], r['Total'][1])
assert p == Rational(24, 55)
assert value(choices[answer]) == p
assert all(value(choices[k]) != p for k in choices if k != answer)
